behavior: Walks through shallow intertidal water and exposed flats, finding bivalves by sight and opening them by stabbing between the shells or hammering them apart. Often rests at communal roosts around high tide and gives loud piping calls during courtship and territorial encounters.
field_marks: Large, thickset shorebird with a robust neck and long legs
Black head, neck, and upper breast
Dark brown back and folded wings contrasting with a white belly
Golden-yellow eye surrounded by a red orbital ring
White wing stripe and white tail base visible in flight
habitat: Strictly coastal intertidal habitats, including sandy or shell beaches, tidal mudflats, saltmarshes, rocky shores, shellfish reefs, dunes, and low islands used for nesting or roosting.
